title: Adaptive reservation shifting and retroactive SLA true-up for dedicated pools
creator: Rafael Kim
description:
Problem statement: Customers on Dedicated pools expect predictable reserved throughput with a clear burst allowance and fair SLA credits when pools degrade or when capacity is rebalanced. Current ledger logic credits SLA refunds at pool-level granularity and uses a simple per-minute snapshot that can over- or under-credit tenants when we temporarily shift reserved throughput between tenants to accomodate bursts. This causes operator overhead, customer disputes, and occasional double-counting in retrospective reconciliations.

Goal: Implement an 'adaptive reservation shift' layer that safely loans unused reserved throughput between tenants in the same pool for short windows, and a deterministic retroactive true-up that assigns SLA credits proportionally based on actual effective reservation during any degraded interval. The system should be auditable, reversible, and cheap to compute at end-of-day reconciliation.

Key design constraints: must be deterministic (replayable from event stream), compatible with existing billing exports, and not increase tail latency. Changes should be feature-flagged per-pool for gradual rollout.

High-level algorithm:
- Track per-tenant reservation weight W_t and active usage U_t sampled at 1s resolution in the serving runtime telemetry. Maintain a sliding window S (default 5m) of recent utilization and idle capacity.
- If pool-wide free reserved capacity > threshold T (default 10% of pool reservation) and tenant A has sustained burst request above its reservation for >= burst_grace (default 30s), loan a fraction L of free reserved capacity to tenant A for a loan TTL (default 2m). Record an event LoanIssued(pool, from_pool_free, to_tenant, amount, start_ts, ttl) in the event ledger.
- Loans are tracked as overlay allocations (soft reservations) and do not change tenant's nominal reservation in the canonical reservation table. They are accounted for in a lightweight loan ledger that is append-only and replayable.
- If pool later suffers a partial degradation (node OOM or capacity loss) affecting the loan period, compute effective reservation for each tenant for the impacted interval by replaying reservation events (nominal reservation + overlay loans that were active at the time). Use this effective reservation to calculate SLA shortfall proportions.
- SLA credits: calculate per-tenant proportional shortfall of effective reservation vs observed served throughput during degraded intervals, then credit SLA tokens proportionally, ensuring that the sum of tenant credits equals the pool-level SLA budget.

Example: pool reservation 1000qps. Tenant A reserved 200qps, Tenant B 300qps, rest unreserved 500qps. B is idle and we loan 150qps to A for 2m. During loan period a node fails for 45s removing 200qps effective capacity. Replay shows A had effective reservation 350qps during impacted 45s and served 300qps, shortfall 50qps. B had effective 150qps but served 0qps and shortfall 150qps. Pool-level shortfall 200qps matches node loss. SLA credits are allocated 25% to A and 75% to B based on shortfall, and attached to tenant invoices as prorated SLA tokens.

Auditability and safety: all loan and reservation-change events are serialized into the existing event-sourcing ledger (same storage used by billing recon exports). A reconciliation job replays events to produce a per-tenant time-series of effective reservation; this job runs nightly and emits a delta file used by invoicing and by the console SLA dashboard. Loans are capped per-tenant and per-pool to avoid unbounded exposure. Feature flags and conservative defaults will be used initially to test on low-risk pools.

Backward compatibility: we provide a compatibility translator that reconstructs the legacy pool-level SLA credit calculation for historical billing data to avoid invoice churn. New invoices will include a new breakdown line "Adaptive-reservation adjustments".
updates: 2026-02-20: RFC created. Initial design reviewed with Billing and Serving teams. Action items: create event schema, add loan ledger table, implement replay job prototype.

2026-02-26: Architecture sync. Agreed on sliding window default S=300s and loan TTL=120s. Decided to sample telemetry at 1s for accuracy; aggregation will be done in the replay job to reduce storage costs.
2026-03-03: Prototype for LoanIssued events implemented (PR #1248). Integration tests validate event ordering and idempotency. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1248

2026-03-05: QA noted edge case where overlapping loans across tenants could cause transient negative free capacity; added cap enforcement logic in runtime and a hard reject if cap exceeded. QA test plan updated.

2026-03-10: Reconciliation job (etl-billing/adaptive-replay) MVP landed behind feature flag. Nightly run produced reconciled deltas for two internal test pools. Observed 0.03% discrepancy vs hand-calculated baseline. Next: run on 10% of pools for two weeks.
To do: add invoicing export column, update Console SLA dashboard to surface per-tenant loan history, run performance test at 10k events/s replay throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Event ledger records loan events with correct schema and ordering (unit tests + integration tests)
Reconciliation job produces per-tenant effective reservation time-series that matches canonical simulator for random test vectors (<=0.1% variance)
Nightly billing delta file includes adaptive adjustments column and is consumed by invoicing without schema errors
Console shows per-tenant loan timeline and per-pool aggregate exposure in the UI
Feature flag present to opt pools in/out and rollout on alpha pools with no customer-facing invoices until release toggle removed
testing_plan: Unit tests for loan issuance, cap enforcement, and TTL expiry logic
Integration test injecting synthetic telemetry for 5 tenants into a test pool and asserting final reconciled deltas match expected allocations
Load test for replay job using 48 hours of synthetic events at 10k events/s to validate memory and CPU profile
Chaos test: simulate node removal during active loans and validate SLA true-up matches pool-level shortfall
End-to-end billing dry-run on two non-production billing accounts for one billing cycle
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal alpha (team-only pools) behind feature flag for 1 week
Phase 1: opt-in by 10% of low-risk customer pools for 2 weeks; run reconciliation in dry-run mode and review deltas
Phase 2: enable invoicing export for opt-in pools and surface adjustments in Console (billing view) for feedback
Phase 3: default-on for all Dedicated pools after 6 weeks and stakeholder sign-off
Rollback plan: disable feature flag + replay compensating negative loan events and re-run reconciliation; invoices hold until compensating run completes
schema_changes: New table: billing.loan_ledger (columns: event_id, pool_id, tenant_id, type, amount, start_ts, ttl_seconds, created_at, metadata)
New Kafka topic: billing.loans.events for realtime streaming to reconciliation service
